name: Energy and Infrastructure
summary: Project-financed power generation (contracted solar, wind and storage; tolled or merchant gas; behind-the-meter power islands; contracted baseload and nuclear PPAs), transmission and midstream, concessions/PPP/availability-payment and regulated-tariff assets, and carbon capture and CO2 storage. A non-recourse SPV borrows against contracted cash flows; lenders rely on the contract suite (PPA/toll/lease, EPC, O&M/LTSA, interconnection, fuel, site control, tax-credit transfer, concession, CO2 transport-and-storage, hedges) and an independent engineer. The diligence spine: delivered power (executed interconnection with upgrades funded, security posted and milestones met, not merely signed), contracted revenue that outlasts the debt from a creditworthy counterparty, debt sized by DSCR on a downside case (S&P 2022 Table 8 by OPBA, Fitch 'BBB' one-year P90 rating case for renewables, 10th-percentile spark spread for merchant gas, DBRS for merchant), a DSRA that survives the downside, firm fuel and winterization, firm (not reserved) equipment with provenance, and tax-credit, FEOC, appropriation and concession-renegotiation risk modelled as variables. Pre-FID, construction and operating dollars are priced separately.
one_check: Delivered power and contracted revenue sized to a downside case: an executed interconnection with upgrades funded, security posted and milestones met; an offtake that outlasts the debt from a creditworthy counterparty; and DSCR that clears the S&P Table 8 range for its risk class on a one-year P90 or 10th-percentile spark-spread case, with a DSRA that survives the downside.

subtypes.name: Contracted solar PV (and solar plus storage)
subtypes.description: Utility or corporate PPA; binding risks are resource (P50 vs one-year P90), curtailment, basis and 45Y/48E tax-credit and FEOC eligibility.

subtypes.name: Contracted wind
subtypes.description: PPA-backed wind; Fitch sets a higher base-case bar (1.60x) because most wind projects underperform P50; time-based availability ~95%.

subtypes.name: Battery / energy storage
subtypes.description: Contracted or tolled storage; shares the renewables contract suite, tax-credit/FEOC exposure and interconnection checks. The bible gives no storage-specific DSCR benchmark; storage is sized off S&P Table 8 by OPBA.

subtypes.name: Contracted thermal / gas (tolling)
subtypes.description: CCGT or peaker under a tolling agreement; the offtaker pays capacity conditioned on availability (Entergy toll 98%/96%); binding risks are availability, heat rate, firm fuel and winterization.

subtypes.name: Merchant or hedged generation
subtypes.description: Spot energy, capacity payments, hedges or revenue puts; binding risks are spark spread / capture price, scarcity events, cannibalization by other announced capacity, capacity-market rules (PJM collar). Panda Temple and Uri are the case files.

subtypes.name: Transmission and midstream (lines, HVDC, pipelines, gas transport)
subtypes.description: Transmission lines, merchant HVDC, renewable energy zones and gas transport assets. The bible covers these mainly through transmission build-rate realism (REPEAT ~1%/yr), network upgrades and firm-transport checks; midstream-specific benchmarks are thin.

subtypes.name: Concession / PPP / availability-payment / regulated tariff
subtypes.description: Revenue set by a public counterparty or regulator (availability payments, tolls, regulated tariffs). Renegotiation is the base rate (54% transport, 74% water in ~1,000 Latin American concessions).

subtypes.name: Carbon capture and CO2 transport/storage
subtypes.description: Capture plants, blue hydrogen, CO2 pipelines and Class VI storage; revenue from offtake, tax credit and transport-and-storage tariffs. A capture plant with no contracted sink is a stranded asset.

subtypes.name: Behind-the-meter power island
subtypes.description: On-site generation (turbines, recips, gensets) serving a data-center tenant under a lease or energy-services contract; binding risks are air permit, fuel, equipment provenance and lead times, and the curtailment interface with the grid. Live deal flow; pair with data-centers.json.

subtypes.name: Contracted baseload / nuclear PPA
subtypes.description: Long-tenor front-of-meter PPAs with hyperscalers (Constellation-Microsoft Crane restart, Talen-AWS 1,920 MW through 2042); binding risks are counterparty and regulatory challenge to cost shifting.

intake_questions.question: What asset is it: contracted solar, wind, storage, tolled thermal, merchant/hedged, transmission or midstream, concession/regulated tariff, CCS, behind-the-meter power island, or contracted baseload/nuclear?
intake_questions.why: Drives which subtype items apply; underwrite the asset you are actually offered (6.1 table).

intake_questions.question: What phase is the capital going into: pre-FID development, construction (FID to COD), or operations? How much of our money is pre-FID?
intake_questions.why: Pre-FID capital is 100% at risk and must be priced like venture, not like a construction loan or operating asset (NZA 2021).

intake_questions.question: Who is the offtaker (utility, corporate, hyperscaler parent or SPV, public body, none), what is the contract (PPA, toll, lease, concession, hedge/revenue put), and what is its tenor against the debt tenor?
intake_questions.why: Sets contracted vs merchant treatment, the merchant tail and the DSCR band (6.2, 6.5).

intake_questions.question: What is the interconnection status: queue filing, cluster study, facilities study, executed LGIA, or energized? Is it reusing an existing (brownfield) interconnection?
intake_questions.why: A queue position is not power; 41% of capacity with signed IAs still withdrew (LBNL 2026).

intake_questions.question: Does the deal's return depend on 45Y, 48E, 45X or other credits, or on transferability? When did (or will) construction begin?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the OBBBA begin-construction, placed-in-service and FEOC checks (6.10).

intake_questions.question: Is any revenue or funding dependent on a government act: appropriation, green bank, ratepayer charge, regulated tariff, capacity-market collar?
intake_questions.why: Triggers sweepability, concession and market-design checks (6.10, 6.11, 11.6).

intake_questions.question: Is the debt rated or to be rated, and what OPBA does the sponsor or its rating adviser expect under S&P 2022?
intake_questions.why: The investment-grade DSCR minimum is a function of OPBA (1.10x to 5.00x).

intake_questions.question: Does the project burn gas or another fuel? Is transport firm or interruptible, and is there on-site backup fuel?
intake_questions.why: Uri: interruptible fuel and curtailable compressors left plants dark (6.7).

intake_questions.question: Does the project serve, or depend on, a data-center customer (behind-the-meter, front-of-meter PPA, or merchant into AI demand)?
intake_questions.why: Pulls in large-load tariff, firm vs curtailable service, parent-guaranty and cannibalization checks (6.4, 6A).

intake_questions.question: Which equipment is on firm order with serial numbers, which is a slot reservation, and is any of it used or refurbished?
intake_questions.why: A slot reservation is a paid option, not equipment (6.4).

requests.request: Deliver a one-page asset and revenue classification memo naming the asset type, what carries the revenue, the binding risk, the capital phase (pre-FID / construction / operating) and the counterparty for every revenue line.
requests.format: Sponsor memo cross-referenced to executed contracts; one row per revenue line.
requests.why: Underwriting a contracted asset when the revenue is actually merchant, or an operating asset when the money is pre-FID.
requests.pass: Every revenue line maps to an executed contract or is labelled merchant; capital phase stated in dollars.
requests.fail: Any revenue line labelled 'contracted' with no executed contract; capital phase not stated.
requests.verify: Tie each line to the executed contract in the data room; compare to 6.1 asset-type table.

requests.request: Provide the executed interconnection agreement (LGIA or equivalent) itself, with all amendments, not a queue printout or summary.
requests.format: Countersigned agreement from the transmission provider/RTO with execution dates; amendments attached.
requests.why: Public queue data often omits or overwrites signed-agreement dates; a queue filing is presented as secured power.
requests.pass: Fully executed LGIA covering the project's MW and point of interconnection, with signed dates.
requests.fail: Queue position, feasibility/system-impact study, or will-serve letter offered instead; unsigned or expired agreement.
requests.verify: Confirm execution and status directly with the transmission provider/RTO and against its public queue record.

requests.request: Provide current queue and cluster status: queue number, cluster assignment, readiness status and readiness deposits posted under FERC Order 2023.
requests.format: RTO/transmission-provider queue record plus deposit receipts.
requests.why: Projects early in the queue carry very low completion base rates (about 19% of projects, 13% of capacity reached COD).
requests.pass: Cluster and readiness status documented by the RTO; deposits posted match the RTO's size-scaled requirement.
requests.fail: No readiness status, deposits not posted, or cluster not identified.
requests.verify: Pull the RTO queue record independently; confirm deposits with the RTO.

requests.request: Provide the executed offtake contract (PPA, tolling agreement, hyperscaler lease, energy-services contract or concession) and a term sheet abstract of tenor, price, termination rights and credit support.
requests.format: Executed agreement with all amendments and side letters; sponsor abstract.
requests.why: Uncontracted revenue sized as contracted; 'single most important document in the file'.
requests.pass: Executed contract in force; abstract ties to the document clause by clause.
requests.fail: LOI, term sheet, or MOU presented as an executed offtake; missing side letters.
requests.verify: Read the full contract; confirm in force with the offtaker in writing.

requests.request: Provide site-control evidence: recorded deed or ground lease/option for every parcel, including access and transmission easements.
requests.format: Recorded instruments and title commitment; parcel map.
requests.why: Projects without site control cannot reach FID; easement gaps strand the interconnection route.
requests.pass: 100% of parcels and easements under recorded control for a term at least equal to debt tenor plus decommissioning.
requests.fail: Unrecorded options, expired options, missing easements or term shorter than debt tenor.
requests.verify: Title search in the county records by our title company.

requests.request: Provide the debt-sizing summary: minimum and average DSCR by case, the OPBA (or rating case) behind it, and how gearing was derived.
requests.format: Model output table signed off by the sponsor's financial adviser.
requests.why: Gearing set first and DSCR backed into; DSCR quoted without the OPBA or rating case behind it.
requests.pass: Debt sized by DSCR sculpting; gearing is an output; minimum DSCR clears the S&P 2022 Table 8 range for the stated OPBA.
requests.fail: Gearing fixed first; single DSCR with no case; minimum DSCR below the Table 8 range; any DSCR below 1.05x.
requests.verify: Recompute from the live model; compare to S&P Table 8 and Fitch indicative table.

requests.request: Provide an equipment status schedule listing each major item (turbines, gensets, transformers, inverters, modules, switchgear) as firm order, slot reservation, delivered or installed, with serial numbers where assigned.
requests.format: Schedule cross-referenced to purchase orders and OEM confirmations.
requests.why: A slot reservation presented as owned turbines.
requests.pass: Every long-lead item on firm purchase order or delivered; serial numbers for delivered items.
requests.fail: Any critical item held only as a reservation slot or option; no serials.
requests.verify: Confirm order status and serials directly with the OEM.

requests.request: State what share of the demand or revenue case is signed contracts, LOIs and forecast, in MW (and MWh) by year.
requests.format: Sponsor table reconciled to executed contracts.
requests.why: A demand case built from a single national or ISO forecast.
requests.pass: Signed contracts cover the debt-sizing case; forecast-only MW excluded from base-case sizing.
requests.fail: Demand case is mostly forecast or LOIs; no split provided.
requests.verify: Tie signed MW to executed contracts.

requests.request: Confirm an independent engineer has been (or will be) appointed by the lenders and provide its engagement letter and scope.
requests.format: Engagement letter naming lender as client; scope covering technology, budget, schedule, availability, heat rate, permits, environmental, projections and draw certification.
requests.why: No independent engineer report.
requests.pass: IE selected by lenders, paid by developer, with full scope including drawdown certification.
requests.fail: No IE, IE engaged by sponsor with no lender reliance, or scope excludes key items.
requests.verify: Call the IE to confirm reliance and scope.

requests.request: State every tax credit (45Y, 48E, 45X, 45Q or other) and transfer/tax-equity structure the returns depend on, with the begin-construction date claimed.
requests.format: Sponsor memo with dollar value per credit by year.
requests.why: A renewable project relying on credits with no begin-construction evidence or FEOC trace.
requests.pass: Every credit identified with dollar value and claimed begin-construction date.
requests.fail: Credit dependence not disclosed or begin-construction date unknown.
requests.verify: Cross-check to the model's tax lines.

requests.request: Provide the proposed financing term sheet: senior debt, tenor, amortization, DSRA, distribution lock-up, covenant DSCR, draw conditions.
requests.format: Lender term sheet or sponsor's proposed terms.
requests.why: Debt terms that cannot survive the downside case.
requests.pass: Debt tenor no longer than contracted tenor or a merchant-tail stress shown; dedicated DSRA; lock-up and covenant DSCR stated.
requests.fail: No DSRA, no lock-up, or tenor exceeding offtake with no tail stress.
requests.verify: Compare to the lenders' documents at confirmatory stage.

requests.request: Deliver the live, unlocked project financial model with all scenarios and a model book.
requests.format: Native Excel, formulas intact, with version log.
requests.why: Black-box models hide backed-into DSCR and optimistic cases.
requests.pass: All cases below run from the same live model and reconcile to contracts and the IE.
requests.fail: Hard-coded outputs, locked sheets, or inconsistent cases.

requests.request: Provide the capital-at-risk curve by month through COD, split into pre-FID, construction (pre-COD) and operating dollars, stating the maximum cumulative exposure before first revenue.
requests.why: Pre-FID dollars priced as if they were construction or operating dollars; pre-FID spend is 100% lost if no FID.
requests.pass: Curve by month; each phase priced separately; pre-FID priced at venture-like returns; maximum exposure stated in the IC memo.
requests.fail: Single blended return across phases; no cash-at-risk curve.
requests.verify: Rebuild from the sources-and-uses and draw schedule.

requests.request: Provide the DSCR table under S&P 2022 Table 8: expected OPBA with reasoning, minimum and average DSCR in base and downside cases.
requests.format: Model output plus rating-adviser memo where available.
requests.why: A 1.70x minimum treated as universal; insufficient coverage for high-OPBA assets.
requests.pass: Minimum DSCR within or above the Table 8 'bbb' range for the expected OPBA (OPBA 1-2: 1.10x-1.20x; 3-4: 1.175x-1.40x; 5-6: 1.30x-1.75x; 7-8: 1.60x-2.50x; 9-10: 2.50x-5.00x); never below 1.05x.
requests.fail: DSCR below the range for the OPBA; OPBA 11-12 presented as investment grade.
requests.verify: Rating adviser or our own OPBA assessment.

requests.request: Provide the S&P downside case and the year in which the DSRA is exhausted.
requests.format: Model downside tab with annual DSCR and DSRA balance.
requests.why: Liquidity reserves depleted by year three ('Low' resiliency).
requests.pass: DSCR above 1.0x in every downside period and mapping to at least 'bbb' in most periods ('very high' resiliency); DSRA not exhausted within debt tenor.
requests.fail: DSRA exhausted by year three, or downside DSCR below 1.0x.
requests.verify: Re-run downside in the live model.

requests.request: Provide the liquidity test: next-12-month sources versus debt service, DSRA sizing, and the covenant headroom under a 10% CFADS decline (OPBA 1-4) or 15% decline (OPBA 5-12).
requests.why: Thin liquidity triggers S&P 'less than adequate' notching.
requests.pass: Sources cover next-12-month debt service at least 1.0x; dedicated DSRA; no covenant breach at the 10%/15% CFADS decline. Strong: sources/uses above 2.0x (OPBA 1-6) or 2.5x (OPBA 7-12) and reserves of 12 months (OPBA 1-6) or 18 months (OPBA 7-12).
requests.fail: Sources below 1.0x, no dedicated DSRA, or covenant breach at the stated decline.

requests.request: Provide the DSRA sizing and funding mechanics (cash or LC, months of debt service, percentage of debt).
requests.why: DSRA below 6 months or no dedicated DSRA.
requests.pass: DSRA at least 6 months (floor); 'stronger' at 12 months of debt service or 5% of total project debt; 18 months for OPBA 7-12 to reach strong liquidity.
requests.fail: Below 6 months, unfunded at COD, or no dedicated DSRA.
requests.verify: Confirm against credit agreement and funding at closing.

requests.request: For renewables, provide DSCR on both the P50 base case and the one-year P90 rating case with availability and O&M haircuts.
requests.format: Model output using the energy-yield report.
requests.why: Renewables debt sized on P50; most wind projects underperform P50.
requests.pass: Debt sized on the one-year P90 rating case. Fitch 'BBB' average DSCR: solar >=1.40x base / >=1.30x rating; wind >=1.60x / >=1.30x; CSP >=1.50x / >=1.40x; biomass/geothermal >=1.60x / >=1.40x.
requests.fail: Sized on P50, or below Fitch rating-case minimum.
requests.verify: Rebuild from the independent energy-yield report.

requests.request: For merchant or partly merchant thermal, provide DSCR at the 10th-percentile spark spread using the market advisor's distribution.
requests.format: Model output with spark-spread distribution inputs.
requests.why: Panda Temple failed on spark spread; a single forward curve hides the tail.
requests.pass: Debt services at P10 spark spread with DSCR clearing S&P OPBA 9-12 rows / DBRS thermal level; DSRA not breached.
requests.fail: Single forward curve; DSCR below 1.0x at P10.

requests.request: Provide the merchant-tail stress: cash flows after the offtake expires through debt maturity, priced at downside merchant prices.
requests.why: A 12-year PPA against an 18-year loan leaves 6 years uncontracted.
requests.pass: Debt amortizes within the contracted tenor, or the tail case DSCR clears the merchant band (>=2.00x for merchant renewables in bank practice; far higher for merchant thermal).

requests.request: Provide the rate sensitivity: equity IRR and DSCR at +200 bp on debt cost and on the discount rate.
requests.why: Clean-energy assets behave like long-duration growth assets; financing costs offset the demand boost.
requests.pass: Sensitivity shown explicitly; debt still sizes and IRR clears hurdle or the gap is disclosed.
requests.fail: Not provided, or covenant breach at +200 bp with no mitigation.

requests.request: Provide the no-credit downside case: equity IRR and whether the debt still sizes if the tax credit is lost or FEOC fails.
requests.why: OBBBA repeal/phase-out or FEOC failure removes credits.
requests.pass: No-credit case shown; debt sizes without the credit or the credit risk is insured/indemnified.
requests.fail: No no-credit case; debt only sizes with the credit and no protection.

requests.request: Provide a 'no new transmission' downside case with curtailment and basis risk applied.
requests.format: Model case with curtailment and basis assumptions.
requests.why: Transmission grows ~1%/yr; projects needing new lines get curtailed.
requests.pass: Case shown for any project whose economics need a new or upgraded line; DSCR survives.
requests.fail: Not provided where network upgrades or new lines are needed.

requests.request: Provide the 'everyone builds' zone price deck: capture prices including other announced and queued capacity in the same zone.
requests.why: Cannibalization: each new plant lowers the clearing price on the whole fleet.
requests.pass: Deck includes other announced capacity; DSCR survives the case where half of it is built.
requests.fail: Deck adds only the sponsor's own MW to today's stack.
requests.verify: Pull the RTO queue for the zone independently.

requests.request: Provide the load/demand case as a distribution, not a point forecast, and list which national-model assumptions (perfect foresight, unconstrained siting, unlimited transmission) it depends on.
requests.why: Models assume perfect foresight; the deal does not.
requests.pass: Distribution provided with downside percentiles; dependency on model assumptions stated.

requests.request: For merchant revenue reliant on PJM (or other) capacity payments, provide a collar-extension case and a collar-expiry case.
requests.why: Today's PJM capacity collar may not persist (cleared ~$16B capped vs ~$26B uncapped).
requests.pass: Both cases shown; debt sizes in the adverse case.

requests.request: Provide the plant model's back-test reproducing historical capacity factor and heat rate before any projection.
requests.format: Model tab comparing modelled vs actual (EIA or plant data).
requests.why: Projections that cannot reproduce history are untrustworthy.
requests.pass: Modelled historical capacity factor and heat rate within a stated tolerance of actual data.
requests.fail: No back-test, or material deviation unexplained.

requests.request: Provide two-way scarcity-event modelling: cost of being short a hedge at the price cap, and default by retail counterparties.
requests.format: Model case at ERCOT-type cap ($9,000/MWh; ancillary up to $25,000/MWh).
requests.why: Uri: plants without fuel owed hedge settlements at the cap.
requests.pass: Scenario shows liquidity survives a multi-day cap event with forced outage; counterparty default modelled.

requests.request: Provide a schedule-realism memo: assumed build rate, EPC crew, transformer, module and turbine availability against historical maxima.
requests.why: National build-rate assumptions far above any historical year (NZA cap 35 GW/yr wind+solar; record 21 GW in 2015).
requests.pass: Schedule consistent with supply-chain evidence; haircut applied where thesis assumes record build rates.

requests.request: Provide the gearing and equity percentage at FID and a reconciliation showing it results from DSCR sculpting.
requests.why: Merchant projects carrying less equity than contracted ones.
requests.pass: Senior debt ~60%-80% of cost for contracted assets as an output of DSCR sizing; merchant carries more equity, not less.
requests.fail: Gearing above the DSCR-sized level; merchant equity below contracted equity.

requests.request: Provide the construction schedule by technology with months from FID to COD and the basis for each.
requests.why: Optimistic build times.
requests.pass: Within benchmarks: solar+storage 12-18 months (or 18-24 per other sources), wind ~2 years, CCGT 3-4 years; deviations justified by the IE.
requests.fail: Schedule shorter than benchmarks without evidence.

requests.request: Provide the energization-timeline stress: debt-service covenants tested against a delayed interconnection/energization date.
requests.why: Interconnection delay destroying economics; ~20% of DC pipeline faces grid delays.
requests.pass: Covenants and liquidity survive the stated delays or delay LDs/funding cover them.

requests.request: Provide the executed PPA with all amendments, and confirm tenor against debt tenor, price and escalation, termination rights, curtailment compensation and change-in-law.
requests.why: Offtake tenor shorter than debt; uncompensated curtailment.
requests.pass: Tenor >= debt tenor (or merchant tail stressed); curtailment compensated; termination rights limited to customary defaults; change-in-law allocated.
requests.fail: Tenor short of debt with no tail stress; offtaker convenience termination; uncompensated curtailment.
requests.verify: Lenders' counsel review; confirm with offtaker.

requests.request: Provide offtaker credit evidence: current ratings, last three years of audited financials, and the credit-support instrument (LC, parent guaranty, collateral).
requests.format: Rating agency reports; audited statements; executed credit support.
requests.why: Weak counterparty makes the contract worthless.
requests.pass: Investment-grade offtaker or credit support from an IG entity covering at least the termination exposure.
requests.fail: Unrated SPV offtaker with no parent guaranty.
requests.verify: Pull ratings directly; confirm LC with issuing bank.

requests.request: Provide the executed tolling agreement with its availability requirement, capacity-payment deduction mechanics and cap.
requests.why: Availability shortfall cuts capacity payments.
requests.pass: Requirement and deductions documented (benchmark Entergy 2020: 98% summer and winter months, 96% other months; 2% payment cut per 1% shortfall, 1% per 1% if force majeure; capped at 100% of monthly payment).

requests.request: For a data-center offtaker, provide the lease/PPA counterparty entity and any parent guaranty showing the hyperscaler parent (not an SPV or JV) owes the payments.
requests.why: SPV/JV tenant with a terminable lease.
requests.pass: Contract with or guaranteed by the IG parent; guaranty scope covers full payment obligations for the debt tenor.

requests.request: Provide a memo on whether the data-center offtaker is hyperscaler-owned or colocation, and on the cost-shifting/ratepayer regulatory exposure of the deal (including behind-the-meter arrangements).
requests.why: Behind-the-meter deals shifting costs to other ratepayers are regulatory risk.
requests.pass: Memo identifies applicable large-load tariff, cost allocation, pending rate cases and challenges; mitigation stated.
requests.fail: No analysis where project serves a data center.

requests.request: Provide comparable hyperscaler baseload PPA terms (e.g., Constellation-Microsoft Crane 20-year; Talen-AWS up to 1,920 MW through 2042) from 8-K filings, benchmarked to this deal.
requests.why: Off-market tenor or price.
requests.pass: Tenor and price within the range of filed comparables or deviation explained.

requests.request: Provide the behind-the-meter lease or energy-services contract with the data-center tenant, including curtailment interface and who runs the load when the grid curtails.
requests.why: Curtailable service sold as firm.
requests.pass: Contract defines firm/non-firm obligations, curtailment hours, backup responsibility and payment during curtailment.

requests.request: Provide all hedge, revenue-put and ISDA documents, including settlement in scarcity events, collateral calls and counterparty credit.
requests.why: Panda Temple's revenue put did not save it; Uri hedge settlements at the cap.
requests.pass: Settlement terms in forced-outage/scarcity events defined; collateral call capacity modelled; counterparty IG.
requests.fail: Unhedged scarcity exposure; uncapped collateral calls.

requests.request: Provide a schedule of capacity-market revenues assumed, with auction results and the rule set (collar, BYOG, backstop) relied on.
requests.format: RTO auction results and model tie-out.
requests.why: Market rules treated as constants.
requests.pass: Every capacity dollar ties to a cleared auction or is in the downside case at zero/collar-expiry.
requests.fail: Uncleared capacity revenue in base case.

requests.request: Provide the executed EPC contract: fixed price, guaranteed completion date, delay LDs and cap, performance guarantees and tests.
requests.format: Executed turnkey fixed-price EPC with schedules.
requests.why: Cost and schedule overrun left on the SPV.
requests.pass: Fixed-price turnkey; delay LDs sized to cover debt service during delay; performance LDs; LD caps customary; completion date before offtake long-stop.
requests.fail: Cost-plus or multi-contract without wrap; LDs below debt service.

requests.request: Provide EPC contractor credit evidence: audited financials, ratings, parent guaranty or performance bond, and a reference list of comparable completed projects.
requests.format: Audited statements; executed guaranty/bond; reference list.
requests.why: Contractor creditworthiness is a critical factor in financeability (Mintz).
requests.pass: Contractor or parent creditworthy for LD exposure; bonded; comparable track record.
requests.fail: Thin contractor with no parent support or no comparable projects.
requests.verify: Call references; verify bond with surety.

requests.request: Provide the executed O&M agreement and/or LTSA with the availability guarantee, its definition (time-based vs energy-based), exclusions and LD cap.
requests.why: Headline percentage hides exclusions and capped LDs.
requests.pass: Gas LTSA availability 95%-98% and at or above the offtake requirement; wind ~95% time-based; exclusions (grid outages, force majeure, scheduled maintenance) read; LD cap meaningful.
requests.fail: Availability below 95%, below the offtake requirement, or broad exclusions.
requests.verify: IE comparison of guarantee vs offtake.

requests.request: Provide a side-by-side reconciliation of the O&M/LTSA availability guarantee against the offtake contract's availability requirement, period by period.
requests.format: Sponsor table signed off by IE.
requests.why: The SPV carries the gap between what the toll demands and what the LTSA guarantees.
requests.pass: Guarantee >= offtake requirement in every period (e.g., 98% summer/winter, 96% other months).
requests.fail: Any period where the guarantee is below the requirement.

requests.request: Provide O&M provider credentials and track record operating comparable plants.
requests.format: Provider statement with fleet list and references.
requests.why: Inexperienced operator erodes availability.
requests.pass: Reputable operator with comparable fleet.

requests.request: Provide the interconnection facilities study and the network-upgrade cost allocation, with the project's share and how it is funded.
requests.format: Facilities study; cost allocation letter; funding evidence.
requests.why: 41% of capacity with signed IAs withdrew; upgrade costs kill projects.
requests.pass: Project's upgrade share quantified, in the budget and funded (substation and network upgrades committed).
requests.verify: Interconnection counsel review; transmission provider confirmation.

requests.request: Provide evidence of interconnection security posted (LCs, cash) and the withdrawal-penalty exposure schedule.
requests.why: Withdrawal penalties and forfeited security.
requests.pass: Security posted in full; withdrawal exposure quantified and in the capital-at-risk curve.

requests.request: Provide the interconnection milestone schedule with the status of each milestone (met, on track, at risk).
requests.format: Schedule with dated evidence for met milestones.
requests.why: Missed milestones trigger withdrawal.
requests.pass: All past milestones met with evidence; future milestones achievable per IE.
requests.fail: Any missed or at-risk milestone without cure.

requests.request: Provide the RTO's FERC Order 2023 compliance posture and any regional variations (e.g., PJM 'reasonable efforts' instead of delay penalties) that affect the cluster study timeline (150-day maximum cluster study).
requests.format: Counsel memo citing the FERC order and RTO compliance filing.
requests.why: Assuming the 150-day study cap applies where the region obtained a variation.
requests.pass: Memo confirms applicable rules from the FERC order and RTO filing.
requests.verify: Read FERC order and RTO compliance filing.

requests.request: Obtain the utility's or RTO's own current interconnection/energization timeline for the specific substation, in writing.
requests.format: Letter or study from the utility/RTO.
requests.why: Sponsors citing 8-12 years or 2 years as a general rule rather than a site-specific study.
requests.pass: Written site-specific timeline; schedule uses it.

requests.request: Provide the post-agreement permitting plan with dates.
requests.format: Permit matrix: permit, agency, status, expected date.
requests.why: Post-agreement permitting delays averaged >14 months in PJM data.
requests.pass: All permits identified; critical-path permits issued or on a schedule consistent with COD with buffer.

requests.request: Provide the transmission owner's procurement schedule for high-voltage transformers for the network upgrades, and the project's own substation transformer purchase order and delivery date.
requests.format: TO letter; executed PO with delivery date.
requests.why: Transformer procurement added nearly 20 months in PJM; transformers are on the critical path twice.
requests.pass: In-service date later than both transformer delivery dates.
requests.fail: In-service date earlier than either delivery date.

requests.request: For brownfield sites, provide evidence of surplus interconnection service or replacement interconnection rights from the retiring unit; otherwise explain why existing interconnection is not reused.
requests.why: Missing the fastest route to grid.
requests.pass: Rights documented or reasoned explanation.
requests.fail: Claimed rights with no RTO documentation.

requests.request: Provide the executed fuel supply agreement: price, volume, term, and flare or direct-line gas feasibility where relevant.
requests.why: Fuel cost and availability risk left on the SPV.
requests.pass: Term covers debt tenor or tolling party supplies fuel; price mechanism matches revenue indexation.
requests.fail: Spot-only supply with no hedge; term short of debt.

requests.request: Provide firm pipeline transport contracts covering maximum daily fuel requirement.
requests.why: Interruptible transport left plants without fuel in Uri.
requests.pass: Firm transport for 100% of the dispatch-case maximum daily quantity.

requests.request: Provide on-site backup fuel capacity (storage volume, hours of full-load run time) and permit allowing backup-fuel operation.
requests.why: Fuel failure in a freeze.
requests.pass: Backup fuel covers a multi-day event consistent with the winterization study.

requests.request: Provide evidence that gas compressors serving the plant are not on the utility's curtailable/load-shed list.
requests.why: Rolling blackouts cut compressor power in Uri.
requests.pass: Compressors designated critical load or self-powered.

requests.request: Provide the winterization plan, the standard it meets, and the funded cost.
requests.why: Generators were urged to winterize after 2011 but did not.
requests.pass: Standard met and cost funded in the budget.

requests.request: Provide firm purchase orders for all long-lead equipment with serial numbers, delivery dates and deposits paid.
requests.format: Executed POs; OEM acknowledgements; proof of deposits.
requests.why: Slot reservations are paid options, not equipment; 13 GW of reservations were cancelled.
requests.pass: Firm PO with delivery dates before required on-site date; deposits evidenced.
requests.fail: Reservation only; delivery after need date.

requests.request: Provide factory acceptance test (FAT per ISO 8528-5 for gensets) and serialized load-bank test certificates for generating equipment.
requests.why: Used/refurbished gensets with no FAT or load-bank certificate.
requests.pass: Certificate per serial for every unit.

requests.request: Provide warranty terms for every major equipment item, distinguishing new, new-surplus and refurbished.
requests.why: Unclear warranty on grey-market equipment.
requests.pass: Warranty term and scope documented; refurbished units carry warranty from a creditworthy party.

requests.request: Provide provenance and pricing for any used or secondary-market turbines (chain of ownership, original order, price per MW).
requests.format: Bill of sale chain; OEM records.
requests.why: Grey-market equipment from failed or cancelled projects.
requests.pass: Clean chain of title; price consistent with ~$1.5M/MW used vs $2M+/MW new benchmark.

requests.request: Provide OEM lead-time confirmation for turbines and gensets relative to the schedule.
requests.why: Lead times: heavy gas turbines 3-7 years; aeroderivatives 18-36 months; gensets >2.5 MW 18-24 months.
requests.pass: Delivery slot confirmed and consistent with COD.
requests.fail: Schedule assumes lead times shorter than benchmarks.

requests.request: Provide all issued permits and the environmental reports (environmental consultant review, environmental impact studies).
requests.why: Serious environmental issues or missing permits.
requests.pass: All construction and operating permits issued or on schedule; no unmitigated environmental issues.

requests.request: Provide the air permit (and backup-generation permit) for fossil generation.
requests.why: Behind-the-meter gas plan with no air permit.
requests.pass: Permit issued covering planned and curtailment-window hours.

requests.request: Provide water source, priority/seniority and cooling design.
requests.format: Water rights, supply contracts, cooling design basis.
requests.why: Water curtailment in arid basins (Colorado River structural deficit ~4M acre-feet/yr).
requests.pass: Senior or contracted firm water supply covering cooling needs; dry-cooling alternative costed.
requests.fail: Junior or undocumented water in an arid market.

requests.request: Provide begin-construction (safe-harbor) evidence: physical-work records or 5% spend documentation.
requests.format: Invoices, contracts, site photos, paid-cost schedule.
requests.why: Credits lost if begin-construction deadlines are missed.
requests.pass: Evidence satisfies current Treasury guidance by the deadline (wind/solar: begin construction before July 2026 with a four-year completion window, or placed in service before 2028, per Kleinman summary).

requests.request: Provide the FEOC supply-chain trace with supplier certifications for every component.
requests.format: Trace report and signed supplier certifications.
requests.why: FEOC material-assistance rules can disqualify projects beginning construction after Dec. 31, 2025.
requests.pass: Trace complete to component level; material-assistance cost ratio passes; certifications signed.
requests.fail: No trace or Chinese-sourced supply/IP unresolved.

requests.request: Provide the tax-credit transfer agreement or tax-equity documents, showing recapture protection and who bears recapture.
requests.why: Recapture lands on the project.
requests.pass: Buyer protected; recapture allocation and indemnity explicit; indemnitor creditworthy or insured.

requests.request: Provide the placed-in-service schedule against credit deadlines and phase-out (phase-out from 2028, ending by 2032 per Kleinman summary).
requests.why: Delay pushes the project past the deadline.
requests.pass: Placed-in-service date has buffer before deadline under current guidance.

requests.request: List every public funding dependency (green bank, ratepayer charge, appropriation, grant) and provide a legal opinion on whether the funds can be swept.
requests.why: Connecticut Green Bank 2018 sweep.
requests.pass: Each dependency identified; sweepability opined; loss-of-funds case modelled.

requests.request: Provide the serving utility's large-load tariff, cost-allocation rules and pending rate cases where the project serves a data center.
requests.why: Ratepayer backlash and tariff change.
requests.pass: All identified and modelled.
requests.fail: No view on rate case or tariff.

requests.request: Provide a market-rule change register: pending RTO/ISO rule changes (capacity collar, large-load proposals, winterization mandates) and their modelled impact.
requests.why: Market rules treated as a constant.
requests.pass: Each pending change named, dated and modelled.

requests.request: Provide the executed concession / PPP / availability-payment agreement.
requests.why: Revenue set by a public counterparty who may want out.
requests.pass: Executed and in force; obligations of grantor clear.

requests.request: Provide the tariff-adjustment formula and the history of every adjustment the counterparty has granted and refused in the last decade.
requests.why: A concession model assuming every scheduled increase is granted; Brazil 1996 refusal.
requests.pass: Track record shows adjustments honored; model haircuts adjustments with poor record.
requests.fail: No record, or model assumes 100% of increases.

requests.request: Provide termination-compensation provisions (default, convenience, force majeure) and a computation showing coverage of senior debt and equity.
requests.why: Payment dependent on appropriation with no termination compensation.
requests.pass: Termination compensation covers at least senior debt in all termination cases.
requests.fail: Compensation below senior debt or absent.

requests.request: Identify which budget line pays the availability payments/tariff, whether it is subject to annual appropriation, and whether it can be swept.
requests.why: Appropriation risk.
requests.pass: Payment from a non-appropriation-dependent source, or appropriation risk mitigated and modelled.

requests.request: Provide the counterparty's election calendar over the debt tenor and any campaign issues involving the project.
requests.why: Political turnover drives renegotiation.
requests.pass: Calendar mapped; no election before COD with project as an issue, or mitigation.
requests.fail: Election before COD with project as a campaign issue.

requests.request: Provide availability-payment deduction definitions, measurement method and cap.
requests.why: Uncapped deductions.
requests.pass: Definitions objective; deductions capped.

requests.request: Provide change-in-law and relief-event provisions.
requests.why: Uncompensated law changes.
requests.pass: Compensation for discriminatory and general change in law; relief events defined.

requests.request: State whether demand/traffic risk is retained (tolls) or transferred (availability payments) and provide the demand study if retained.
requests.why: Demand risk underestimated.
requests.pass: Retained demand risk supported by independent study with downside.
requests.fail: Demand risk retained with no study.

requests.request: Provide the signed CO2 transport-and-storage agreement (or owned Class VI permit) with per-tonne tariff, capacity and monitoring terms.
requests.why: A capture plant with no contracted sink is stranded.
requests.pass: Signed T&S agreement covering full capture volume; tariff ~$17-$23/t stored or justified premium.

requests.request: Provide the Class VI permit status and storage-site characterization (injectivity, capacity, monitoring plan).
requests.why: Storage site not characterized.
requests.pass: Permit issued or on schedule; characterization supports capacity for project life.

requests.request: Provide the credit agreement and intercreditor/accounts agreements: draw conditions, DSRA, distribution lock-up, covenant DSCR and events of default.
requests.why: Weak lender protections.
requests.pass: Lock-up and covenant DSCR set above default levels; DSRA funded; IE draw certification required.
requests.fail: No lock-up; IE not in draw process.

requests.request: Provide bound insurance quotes (not indications) for the full hold, including named-storm, wildfire and freeze terms and deductibles.
requests.format: Binder or bound quotes from insurers/broker.
requests.why: An indication presented as a bound quote; uninsurable assets.
requests.pass: Bound quotes for construction and operations covering lender requirements; named-storm/wildfire/freeze terms stated.
requests.fail: Indications only; coverage from insurer of last resort only.

requests.request: Provide three years of premium history and a 2x premium stress in the model.
requests.why: Premiums repricing through reinsurance.
requests.pass: History provided; DSCR survives 2x premium.
requests.fail: Insurance expense held flat in exposed market.

requests.request: Provide the construction budget with contingency, and the sources and uses.
requests.why: Budget gaps.
requests.pass: Budget reconciles to EPC and owner's costs; contingency reasonable per IE.

requests.request: For merchant or partly merchant assets, provide historical market data for the node/zone: prices, basis, curtailment.
requests.why: Capture price and basis assumptions not grounded.
requests.pass: Assumptions reconcile to historical nodal data.

requests.request: For transmission or midstream assets whose revenue depends on throughput, provide firm transport/transmission service contracts and shipper/user credit.
requests.why: Uncontracted throughput.
requests.pass: Firm contracts cover debt-sizing volume from creditworthy shippers.

requests.request: Provide the corporate structure chart of the SPV, holdco and sponsor with ring-fencing provisions.
requests.why: Non-recourse SPV not ring-fenced.
requests.pass: SPV bankruptcy-remote with separateness covenants.

requests.request: Commission (lender-selected, developer-paid) the Independent Engineer report covering technology, budget, schedule, availability, heat rate, permits, environment and projections.
requests.format: Signed IE report with reliance letter to lenders.
requests.why: No IE report; unrealistic projections.
requests.pass: IE confirms technology commercially viable, budget and schedule reasonable, no serious environmental issues, permits in order, projections realistic.
requests.fail: Qualified or adverse IE findings unresolved.

requests.request: Commission an independent energy-yield report with P50 and one-year P90, curtailment and basis assumptions.
requests.why: Debt sized on optimistic resource.
requests.pass: Report provides P50 and one-year P90; rating case uses one-year P90 with haircuts.

requests.request: Commission a market advisor report with spark-spread and capture-price distributions, the 'everyone builds' zone case and capacity-price collar cases.
requests.why: Single forward curve; cannibalization.
requests.pass: Distributions provided; P10 case used for sizing.

requests.request: Commission interconnection counsel/RTO specialist review of cluster status, readiness deposits, network-upgrade allocation and withdrawal-penalty exposure.
requests.why: Signed IA, project still dies.
requests.pass: No unmitigated interconnection risk.

requests.request: Obtain a tax opinion on begin-construction and placed-in-service deadlines, FEOC material-assistance analysis, transferability and recapture.
requests.why: Credit lost.
requests.pass: Unqualified or 'should' level opinion on eligibility.
requests.fail: Qualified opinion on a gating credit.

requests.request: Commission a supply-chain tracing firm to verify the FEOC trace and supplier certifications.
requests.why: Self-certified supply chains.
requests.pass: Independent trace matches sponsor trace.

requests.request: Commission a weather and winterization engineer: winterization standard compliance and a freeze-event dispatch study.
requests.why: Uri fuel and equipment failure.
requests.pass: Plant and fuel chain operate through a design freeze event.

requests.request: Commission regulatory and political-risk counsel on tariff-adjustment history, termination compensation and appropriation sweep risk.
requests.why: Renegotiation and sweep.
requests.pass: Risks identified and mitigated.

requests.request: Commission water-rights counsel on source, seniority and curtailment priority.
requests.why: Junior water curtailed.
requests.pass: Senior or firm contracted water.
requests.fail: Junior rights in arid basin unmitigated.

requests.request: Commission a storage geologist on injectivity, capacity, monitoring plan and Class VI status.
requests.why: Storage site fails.
requests.pass: Capacity and injectivity support project life.

requests.request: Obtain the rating adviser's view of expected OPBA and the downside case under S&P 2022.
requests.why: DSCR quoted without OPBA.
requests.pass: OPBA and downside consistent with sizing.

requests.request: Commission an environmental consultant report (site environmental conditions and permitting).
requests.why: Serious environmental issue.
requests.pass: No unmitigated issue.

requests.request: Commission an insurance advisor review of the program and bound quotes.
requests.why: Underinsurance.
requests.pass: Program meets lender requirements.

requests.request: Commission an equipment inspector to witness FAT and verify serial numbers and load-bank certificates.
requests.why: Grey-market or undocumented equipment.
requests.pass: All units verified.

requests.request: Commission an independent model audit.
requests.why: Formula errors and backed-into DSCR.
requests.pass: Clean audit; cases reconcile.

requests.request: Obtain project-finance counsel's legal due diligence report on the contract suite.
requests.why: Contract gaps across the suite.
requests.pass: No material gaps.

requests.request: Obtain the IE's closing certificate confirming conditions precedent (budget, schedule, permits, contracts) are satisfied.
requests.why: Closing on stale diligence.
requests.pass: Certificate unqualified.

requests.request: Provide bound insurance certificates at closing naming lenders as loss payees/additional insureds.
requests.why: Coverage gap at closing.
requests.pass: Bound and endorsed.

requests.request: Evidence the DSRA funded (cash or LC) at closing or at COD as required.
requests.why: Unfunded reserve.
requests.pass: Funded at the required level.

requests.request: Confirm interconnection security posted and milestones current as of closing.
requests.why: Lapsed interconnection.
requests.pass: Current and in good standing.

requests.request: Deliver executed tax-credit transfer/tax-equity documents and final tax opinion at closing.
requests.why: Credit monetization fails.
requests.pass: Executed with recapture protection.

requests.request: Deliver legal opinions (enforceability, security, regulatory) and executed direct agreements/consents with each major counterparty (offtaker, EPC, O&M, interconnection, concession grantor).
requests.why: Lenders cannot step in.
requests.pass: All direct agreements executed.

requests.request: Deliver the executed parent guaranty or credit support for offtake, EPC and O&M obligations.
requests.why: Unsupported obligations.
requests.pass: Executed by the rated parent.

requests.request: Provide IE drawdown certifications for each construction draw against physical progress.
requests.why: Draws ahead of progress.
requests.pass: Each draw certified.

requests.request: Provide monthly construction reports against the schedule, interconnection milestones and equipment deliveries.
requests.why: Silent slippage.
requests.pass: On schedule or variance explained with cure.

requests.request: Provide quarterly DSCR covenant compliance certificates and DSRA balances.
requests.why: Covenant breach (Panda Temple breached its DSRA covenant).
requests.pass: DSCR above covenant and lock-up; DSRA full.

requests.request: Provide monthly availability, capacity factor and heat-rate reports against guarantees and offtake requirements.
requests.why: Availability shortfall cuts revenue.
requests.pass: Availability >= guarantee and offtake requirement.

requests.request: Provide quarterly energy production versus P50/P90.
requests.why: Persistent underperformance (wind vs P50).
requests.pass: Production at or above P90.

requests.request: Provide placed-in-service evidence and annual credit compliance/recapture monitoring.
requests.why: Recapture.
requests.pass: Compliant.

requests.request: Provide quarterly updates on market-rule changes, rate cases, tariff adjustments and appropriations affecting revenue.
requests.why: Rule change unnoticed.
requests.pass: Updates provided and modelled.

requests.request: Provide renewal terms and premiums at each renewal against the model.
requests.why: Premium shock.
requests.pass: Within model or stress case.

requests.request: Provide monthly hedge mark-to-market and collateral posting reports.
requests.why: Collateral calls drain liquidity.
requests.pass: Collateral within liquidity.

requests.request: Provide CO2 injection and monitoring reports under the Class VI permit.
requests.why: Storage failure or leakage.
requests.pass: Within permit.

requests.request: Provide winter readiness certification before each winter season.
requests.why: Freeze failure.
requests.pass: Certified.

requests.request: Provide annual counterparty credit updates for offtaker, EPC/O&M and hedge counterparties.
requests.why: Counterparty deterioration.
requests.pass: No downgrade below required level.

kill_tests.test: No independent engineer report, or the IE has no lender reliance.
Power evidenced only by a queue position, feasibility study or will-serve letter, with no executed interconnection agreement.
Critical generating equipment held only as a slot reservation with no firm purchase order.
Contracted subtype with no executed offtake contract.
Minimum DSCR below the S&P 2022 Table 8 range for the asset's OPBA, or any period below 1.05x in the base case.
Renewables debt sized on P50 with no one-year P90 rating case.
No dedicated DSRA, or DSRA below 6 months of debt service.
Merchant thermal sized at a merchant-renewables DSCR, or no DSCR test at the 10th-percentile spark spread.
Availability guarantee below the offtake contract's requirement or below 95%.
Gas supply on interruptible transport with no backup fuel, or compressors on the curtailable list.
Credit-dependent project with no begin-construction evidence or no FEOC trace.
Capture project with no contracted CO2 sink or owned Class VI permit.
Concession payment dependent on annual appropriation with no termination compensation.
Sponsor refuses to provide the executed interconnection agreement itself or the live model.

red_flags.flag: A queue position filing presented as secured power.
red_flags.check: Obtain the executed LGIA and confirm with the RTO.

red_flags.flag: A slot reservation presented as owned turbines.
red_flags.check: Firm PO, serial numbers, OEM confirmation.

red_flags.flag: A merchant project with contracted-level DSCR.
red_flags.check: Map to S&P OPBA 7-12 / DBRS; size at P10 spark spread.

red_flags.flag: Used or refurbished gensets with no FAT, no serialized load-bank certificate, and unclear warranty.
red_flags.check: Equipment inspector witness FAT and certificates by serial.

red_flags.flag: No independent engineer report.
red_flags.check: Lender-appointed IE with reliance.

red_flags.flag: An executed LGIA presented as certainty of COD, with no network-upgrade cost allocation, posted security, or milestone status.
red_flags.check: Obtain all three; 41% of signed capacity withdrew.

red_flags.flag: An interconnection agreement with no permitting plan and no transformer procurement schedule.
red_flags.check: Request both; in-service date after both transformer deliveries.

red_flags.flag: A data-center site marketed as having 'secured power' whose service is non-firm or curtailable.
red_flags.check: Written firm/non-firm terms and hourly curtailment study.

red_flags.flag: A 'fast-track' data-center interconnection with no written non-firm or flexible service terms and no curtailment study.
red_flags.check: Utility's written terms and site-specific study.

red_flags.flag: A renewable project relying on credits with no begin-construction evidence or FEOC trace.
red_flags.check: Safe-harbor evidence, FEOC trace, tax opinion.

red_flags.flag: A demand case built from a single national or ISO load forecast with no distribution and no competing-supply case.
red_flags.check: Distribution and 'everyone builds' case.

red_flags.flag: Pre-FID development dollars priced as if they were construction or operating dollars.
red_flags.check: Capital-at-risk curve; separate pricing.

red_flags.flag: A sponsor citing the 8-to-12-year or the 2-year timeline as a general rule, rather than a site-specific utility study.
red_flags.check: Written utility/RTO timeline for the substation.

red_flags.flag: Gearing set first and DSCR backed into, or a DSCR quoted without the OPBA or rating case behind it.
red_flags.check: Rebuild sizing from DSCR sculpting.

red_flags.flag: Renewables debt sized on P50 rather than a one-year P90 rating case.
red_flags.check: Re-size on one-year P90.

red_flags.flag: A merchant thermal plant at a merchant-renewables DSCR (DBRS: thermal needs roughly three times).
red_flags.check: Size off S&P OPBA 9-12 and P10 spark spread.

red_flags.flag: A DSRA below 6 months, or no dedicated DSRA.
red_flags.check: Credit agreement and funding evidence.

red_flags.flag: An availability guarantee below 95%, or one that sits below the offtake contract's availability requirement.
red_flags.check: Side-by-side reconciliation.

red_flags.flag: Gas supply on interruptible transport with no backup fuel, or compressors on the curtailable list.
red_flags.check: Firm transport contracts; critical-load letter.

red_flags.flag: A merchant revenue model that assumes today's PJM capacity collar persists, with no collar-expiry case.
red_flags.check: Collar-expiry case.

red_flags.flag: A concession with no record of tariff adjustments actually granted.
red_flags.check: Decade history of adjustments granted and refused.

red_flags.flag: A concession model that assumes every scheduled tariff increase is granted.
red_flags.check: Haircut adjustments to the track record.

red_flags.flag: Payment dependent on annual appropriation with no termination compensation.
red_flags.check: Budget line and termination clause.

red_flags.flag: A counterparty facing an election before COD with the project as a campaign issue.
red_flags.check: Election calendar memo.

red_flags.flag: A capture project with no contracted CO2 sink.
red_flags.check: Signed T&S agreement or Class VI permit.

red_flags.flag: Equity pushed lower for merchant than for contracted assets.
red_flags.check: Merchant should carry more equity; recompute.

red_flags.flag: Project in-service date earlier than the transformer delivery dates (own substation or TO network upgrades).
red_flags.check: Compare dates.

red_flags.flag: Hyperscaler offtake signed by an SPV or JV with a terminable lease and no parent guaranty.
red_flags.check: Read the guaranty.

red_flags.flag: Program funded by a green bank, ratepayer charge or appropriation with no sweepability analysis.
red_flags.check: Counsel opinion; loss case.

red_flags.flag: Load-growth-lowers-rates studies used to dismiss ratepayer backlash risk.
red_flags.check: Treat as spare-capacity-era evidence; model tariff change.

red_flags.flag: Insurance indication presented as a bound quote, or premium held flat in an exposed market.
red_flags.check: Bound quote; 2x stress.

hard_questions.question: Show the executed interconnection agreement and the substation funding, the network-upgrade cost allocation, the security posted, the milestone schedule and status, the permitting plan and the transformer delivery dates.
hard_questions.good_answer: All seven documents produced from the data room within a day, with the in-service date after both transformer deliveries and every milestone met.

hard_questions.question: Is the power contracted, for how long, and against what debt tenor?
hard_questions.good_answer: Executed offtake with tenor at or beyond debt maturity, or a merchant-tail case that still covers debt service.

hard_questions.question: Is the equipment firm-ordered and inspected, or a reservation?
hard_questions.good_answer: Firm POs with serials and FAT/load-bank certificates witnessed by an inspector.

hard_questions.question: What is the DSCR in the merchant or downside case, and what is the DSRA?
hard_questions.good_answer: A downside table already built, DSCR above 1.0x every period, DSRA of at least 6 months (ideally 12).

hard_questions.question: What OPBA do you expect S&P to assign, and does your minimum DSCR clear the Table 8 range for it? In the downside case, in which year is the DSRA exhausted?
hard_questions.good_answer: A rating-adviser memo naming the OPBA, minimum DSCR inside the range, and a DSRA that is never exhausted within tenor.

hard_questions.question: Is the energy case P50 or one-year P90? Show both DSCRs.
hard_questions.good_answer: Both shown; debt sized on one-year P90 clearing Fitch's rating-case minimum.

hard_questions.question: What does the availability guarantee define as 'available', what is excluded, and what is the LD cap? Does it match the offtake contract's requirement?
hard_questions.good_answer: Definition and exclusions quoted, LD cap stated, guarantee at or above offtake requirement every month.

hard_questions.question: Is the service firm or curtailable? If curtailed, what runs the load, under what permit, and for how many hours?
hard_questions.good_answer: Written firm terms, or an hourly curtailment study with backup sized and air-permitted for the hours.

hard_questions.question: What has the queue done to your cluster? What is your withdrawal-penalty exposure?
hard_questions.good_answer: Current cluster status from the RTO and a dollar withdrawal exposure already in the capital-at-risk curve.

hard_questions.question: Who pays for network upgrades and incremental capacity costs, and is that in the lease or PPA?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named party per cost with the clause reference.

hard_questions.question: How much of your capital is pre-FID, how much pre-COD, and what is the maximum cumulative cash at risk before first revenue?
hard_questions.good_answer: A monthly cash-at-risk curve with peak exposure stated and pre-FID priced at venture returns.

hard_questions.question: How many MW of other generation are announced or in the queue in your zone, and what happens to your capture price if half of it is built?
hard_questions.good_answer: A zone queue list and a price deck with the half-built case still servicing debt.

hard_questions.question: If the tax credit disappears or the FEOC test fails, what is the equity IRR and does the debt still size?
hard_questions.good_answer: A no-credit case run before being asked; debt sizes or credit loss is insured/indemnified.

hard_questions.question: What happens in a Uri-type freeze: where does the fuel come from, and what do you owe on your hedges at the cap?
hard_questions.good_answer: Firm transport plus on-site backup for X days, compressors on critical load, and a computed hedge exposure covered by liquidity.

hard_questions.question: What is the IRR at +200 bp on debt and discount rate?
hard_questions.good_answer: Sensitivity table already in the model.

hard_questions.question: Does the site reuse an existing interconnection? If not, why not?
hard_questions.good_answer: Yes with RTO documentation, or a reasoned explanation.

hard_questions.question: Show every tariff adjustment the counterparty has granted and refused in the last decade.
hard_questions.good_answer: A dated list from public records, with the model haircutting increases to that record.

hard_questions.question: What do we receive on termination for convenience?
hard_questions.good_answer: At least senior debt plus a defined equity return, paid from a non-appropriation source.

hard_questions.question: Which budget line pays, and can it be swept?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named line with a counsel opinion that it cannot be swept, or a modelled loss case.

hard_questions.question: Where does each tonne of CO2 go, under what signed agreement, at what tariff, and who owns the injection permit?
hard_questions.good_answer: A signed T&S agreement for full volume at ~$17-$23/t (or justified premium) and a named Class VI permit holder.

hard_questions.question: Which assumptions of the national model you cite (perfect foresight, unconstrained siting, unlimited transmission) does the project depend on?
hard_questions.good_answer: A list and a downside case without them.

failure_cases.what_happened: 758 MW ERCOT CCGT financed with ~$377M debt and $375M equity filed Chapter 11 in April 2017 after breaching its DSRA covenant; low spark spreads despite a revenue-put hedge.
failure_cases.check: Contracted offtake; merchant-tail stress; DSRA sizing; spark-spread distributions; DSCR at P10 spark spread; model reproduces historical capacity factor.

failure_cases.what_happened: Merchant coal plant filed Chapter 11 in January 2017.

~30 GW missing vs ~45 GW non-summer load; prices at $9,000/MWh cap, ancillaries $25,000/MWh; ~$140B losses (~$50B ERCOT charges, ~$90B P&C); gas compression failed as blackouts cut compressor power; winterization not paid for or enforced.
failure_cases.check: Firm transport, on-site backup fuel, compressors off curtailable list; winterization standard and cost; two-way scarcity modelling.
